home.title: Multi-Species Mutant
home.subtitle: SoyMutDB is a comprehensive multi-species mutant database (soybean as the first/default species) providing massive variant data, gene information, mutant resources, and a genome browser to advance plant functional genomics research.
home.featuresSubtitle: Comprehensive bioinformatics tools for multi-species plant research
home.featureGenomeBrowserDesc: Interactive genome browser based on JBrowse 2 with multi-track visualization and deep linking.
home.featureVariantSearchDesc: Powerful variant search with filtering by gene, region, impact, mutation type, and more.
home.featureBlastDesc: Fast sequence alignment tool supporting nucleotide and protein searches.
home.featureAnalyticsDesc: Rich statistical charts and visual analysis to explore variant data in depth.
home.featureSeedsDesc: Rich mutant seed resources with online application and MTA support.
home.featureDocumentationDesc: Comprehensive documentation and API reference to get started with SoyMutDB.
home.dataOverviewDesc: Genome-wide variant distribution and impact classification
home.latestReleaseDesc: Latest data release with more mutant lines and improved annotation quality.

analyticsSettings.title: Analytics Settings
analyticsSettings.description: Visitor statistics for the public portal via Cloudflare Web Analytics.
analyticsSettings.overviewDesc: Cloudflare Web Analytics is a free, privacy-first, cookie-free traffic analytics service. The portal (apps/web) loads it through a single static JavaScript beacon embedded at build time — no Workers, KV or D1 involved, so the deployment stays pure static hosting.
analyticsSettings.beaconNote: Only the public portal (apps/web) loads the beacon; this admin console and the JBrowse app do not.
analyticsSettings.configDesc: The beacon token is a VITE_* variable injected at BUILD time into the portal HTML. This page is a documentation-only interface: it does not store the token, does not call the backend, and cannot change the running site.
analyticsSettings.envVarHelp: Set it in the Cloudflare Pages project "soymutdb-web" → Settings → Environment variables, for both Production and Preview. Values cannot be read back from the dashboard after saving.
analyticsSettings.step1Desc: Cloudflare Dashboard → Analytics & Logs → Web Analytics → Add a site. Pick the portal domain (e.g. www.example.com). No DNS/proxy change is required — the beacon works on any static host.
analyticsSettings.step2Desc: Open the installation snippet of the new site and copy the token from data-cf-beacon (a short hex string).
analyticsSettings.step3Desc: In the soymutdb-web Pages project: Settings → Environment variables → Add variable VITE_CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN with the token value (Production and Preview), then redeploy.
analyticsSettings.step4Desc: Trigger a new production deployment so the token is baked into the built index.html. Older deployments created before the variable was added contain no beacon.
analyticsSettings.step5Desc: Open the portal and view the page source: it should contain static.cloudflareinsights.com/beacon.min.js. Traffic then appears in Cloudflare Dashboard → Web Analytics (may take a few minutes).
analyticsSettings.statusDesc: The token is injected into the portal HTML at build time, so this page cannot detect the current injection state at runtime (the admin bundle never carries the value). Use the checks below instead.
analyticsSettings.statusHint1: Open the portal in a browser → View page source (Ctrl/Cmd+U) → search for "cloudflareinsights". Found means the beacon is injected in the current deployment.
analyticsSettings.statusHint2: Or check Cloudflare Dashboard → Web Analytics: if the site shows traffic shortly after a deployment, the beacon is working.
analyticsSettings.legacyDesc: The API-side ClickHouse analytics endpoint and the portal /analytics page remain available as a fallback / detail source. Cloudflare Web Analytics is the primary visitor-statistics channel.
